Concentration-round first-touch: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:engine` (lands in `packages/drivers/driver-sql` tests).

Pinned-premise test per the card's own shape and the #7738 precedent: assert the `asc === desc` signature over an unprovisioned injected anchor on the federated SQLite harness, **plus the reversing baseline on a real column** — the card is right that the baseline leg is load-bearing (without it a driver that stopped sorting entirely stays green). Purpose on record: the #10474 lint WARNING's justification becomes red-on-change instead of silently stale if either door ever starts refusing this ORDER BY. Size S, test-only.

Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, test-only
Clause-②: **no** — this pins existing behaviour and changes none.
Serial constraints cleared: same **package** as in-flight #11101, **different file**. Under this seat's serialization rule as of today that is not a conflict; see the note below. ⛔ If your work turns out to need an edit to `sql-driver.ts`, that is a breach — stop and report, do not edit it.

## What this card is, stated precisely

It is **not** a bug fix. Nothing here is broken by intent — the card pins a *premise* that another gate's justification rests on. `#10474` shipped `sort-field-unprovisioned`, an author-time WARNING about ordering a list view by a registry-injected anchor on an ADR-0015 `external` object. That warning's entire warrant is a runtime fact: **neither runtime door refuses such an ORDER BY**, so the authoring gate is the only door there is.

Nothing asserts that fact. So if either door ever starts refusing, the lint warning silently becomes wrong — describing a silent degradation that no longer happens, on a path that is now a loud `400` — and nothing turns red. Triage's first-touch put it exactly right: *"the #10474 lint WARNING's justification becomes red-on-change instead of silently stale."*

The two doors, both narrowing on `formula` alone and therefore both letting an injected `datetime`/`lookup` anchor through:
- `assertSortFieldsExist` — `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (#6994), third verdict filters `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES`
- `assertOrderByIsMaterializable` — `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (#7095), `schema.fields[f]?.type === 'formula'`

⛔ **Read both, but edit neither.** Confirming the narrowing is still `formula`-only is part of the job; changing it is not this card's business at all.

## The measured signature to pin

From the card, measured on `claude/issue-10474-sort-axis-provenance` with a real `SqlDriver` over better-sqlite3, against a remote table carrying none of the injected anchors:

```
orderBy name       asc -> [c1,c2,c3]   desc -> [c3,c2,c1]   (a real column: reverses)
orderBy created_at asc -> [c1,c2,c3]   desc -> [c1,c2,c3]   asc === desc, 3 rows, no error
orderBy owner_id   asc -> [c1,c2,c3]   desc -> [c1,c2,c3]   asc === desc, 3 rows, no error
```

**Both legs are required and the baseline is the load-bearing one.** `asc === desc` alone is satisfied by a driver that stopped sorting entirely; the reversing control on a real column is what makes it a *dropped sort* rather than a coincidence. Triage agreed on the record. ⛔ Do not ship the anchor legs without the control.

Suggested home: beside `sql-driver-external-remote-name.test.ts`, which already carries the federated SQLite harness. Object declared as `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/external/customer.object.ts` declares it, remote table `[id, name, email, region, lifetime_value]`.

## Write the header so the next reader knows what a red means

This is a **premise pin**, and its failure mode is unusual: going red does not necessarily mean someone broke something — it may mean someone *fixed* the runtime and the #10474 lint rule now needs retiring or re-levelling. Say that in the file header, in the style of `packages/objectql/src/engine-external-tenant-scope.test.ts` (#7738), which is the precedent this card names and which states its own premise-pin role in its header. A premise pin whose red is misread as a regression gets "fixed" by restoring the very defect it documents.

## ⛔ Boundaries

- ⛔ `sql-driver.ts` belongs to in-flight #11101. ⛔ `protocol.ts` and `objectql/src/engine.ts` are read-only for you; both are also carrying open PRs in this lane.
- ⛔ `packages/spec` off limits. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`.
- ⛔ Do not "fix" the unprovisioned-anchor behaviour. The card pins it deliberately; the #3821 backstop returning rows unordered under a success is the documented status quo, and changing it needs its own ruling.
- ⛔ New test files in `packages/**` that declare an engine double must route `update()`/`delete()` through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`/`assertEngineDeleteDispatch` (import from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, never from `objectql` — that edge is a cycle turbo refuses), or `check:engine-double-contract` fails the build. A lane PR went red on exactly this today. You are likely using the real driver rather than a double, in which case it does not arise — but check before pushing.

## Context worth having

The card records why no sweep caught this: `examples/app-showcase` declares two federated objects and **no list view, view record or page binds either of them**, so the federated read path has no authored SORT or SEARCH surface anywhere in the examples. That is also why your fixture has to construct the situation rather than find it.

## Note on serialization

Dispatching this alongside #11101 in one package would not have happened an hour ago — this seat was serializing on same-package. The repo's own `scripts/check-single-claim-paths.mjs` measures shared-path concurrency at **68 pairs per 300 PRs** and calls it "ordinary concurrent work", declaring exactly one at-most-one-writer path (`.objectui-sha`). The rule is now same-**file**, which is why two disjoint files in `driver-sql` can run in parallel — and why `sql-driver.ts` is a hard boundary for you rather than a soft one.

## ACCEPT — PR #11165, 34/34 checks green, enqueued

Verified by name: every run `success` or `skipped`, including `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`. `Console Pin Gate` skipped, not red. Flipped to ready, auto-merge enabled.

**The control was proved, not asserted — and that is the part worth keeping.** The dispatch told you the baseline leg was load-bearing. You did not take that on my authority; you measured it with a second reverse-verification leg:

| mutation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| remote table really carries `created_at` ("someone fixed the runtime") | anchor red, control green | `3 failed \| 8 passed` — FIXTURE, the `created_at` anchor, and MECHANISM red; control + the other six anchors green |
| control's column made unresolvable ("no sort applied at all") | control red, anchors green | `1 failed \| 10 passed` — **only** the control |

Leg B is the recorded proof that under a total sort loss every anchor leg stays green and the control is the only thing that notices. A control defended by argument can be deleted by the next reader who finds the argument unconvincing; a control with a measurement attached cannot.

Three more things done right:

- **The anchor list is derived, not typed.** Taking the seven from the spec's own `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` and the served field set from `injectedSystemColumnDefs` means a future ADR that adds or removes an anchor is covered without anyone remembering to update a hand-maintained list. That is the difference between a pin and a snapshot.
- **The mechanism is recorded from the emitted SQL**, because *"the sort was never issued"* and *"the sort was issued and dropped"* are different facts and only one of them is what the #10474 warning rests on. Pinning the two statements — the `order by` that SQLite rejects, then the #3821 ladder's bare retry — pins the actual claim.
- **The fixture is copied rather than imported**, with the reason stated: a test reading outside its own package is invisible to turbo's affected set and to the `test` task's input hashing. It is a fixture of that shape, not a mirror — so it cannot silently stop running when the showcase app changes.

The header stating both readings of a future red is exactly what this card was for. A premise pin misread as a regression gets "fixed" by restoring the defect it documents; naming the second reading — *someone widened a door, so retire or re-level `sort-field-unprovisioned` and delete these cases* — is what prevents that.

### On the two deviations you flagged

Both were the right call and neither needed my approval:

1. **`skip-changeset` instead of a changeset.** My dispatch line asked for a changeset generically; this repo refuses an empty-frontmatter one (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`), and `skip-changeset` is the mechanism for a test-only PR that publishes nothing. `Check Changeset` went **green** on the strength of it. **Label race checked, as you asked** — current state is `["size/m", "tests", "skip-changeset"]`, so the size labeler's PUT did not drop it. Good instinct to ask for the second read rather than trusting your own write-back.
2. **`check:query-options-erasure` fixed in your own new code.** The ratchet reported `test surface grew 240 → 242` and you satisfied it the way it prescribes — a typed `DriverQuery` local instead of `{...} as any` — returning it to `240 site(s) in 47 file(s) — at the ceiling`. ⭐ Worth saying plainly: **raising the ceiling would have been the wrong move and I would have sent it back.** A ratchet you widen to get green stops being a ratchet.

No out-of-scope findings, and none forced — the card's premise held on current `main` (both doors re-read, both still narrowing on `formula` alone), and `sql-driver.ts` was read but never written, so the boundary against in-flight #11101 held.
